inputSummary: Fixed Flathub repository enabled-detection library review

findings.description: Scope normalization silently discards custom installation names. _flathub_normalize_scope only recognizes 'system'/'user' tokens; custom installation names (steamdeck, fedora, etc.) from _flathub_probe_installations are dropped → FLATHUB_SCOPE='empty' when Flathub ONLY enabled in custom installation. Violates Claims 3, 17, 20 documented vocabulary.
findings.counterexample: Steam Deck with flathub only in custom 'steamdeck' installation → flathub_enabled=true but flathub_scope='empty'

findings.description: State machine returns 'not-configured' on partial query failure instead of 'unknown'. When one scope (system/user) answers authoritatively with no flathub but other scope fails (timeout/permission), lines 780-785 treat failure as 'no flathub' → false negative.
findings.counterexample: System scope: no flathub (rc=0); User scope: timeout (rc=1) → returns 'not-configured' instead of 'unknown'

findings.description: Positive-only caching lacks TTL/invalidation. _FLATHUB_DETECTED=1 caches 'enabled' forever; no mechanism to invalidate on flatpak remote-disable, admin changes, or config drift. Stale ENABLED persists in long-lived shells (CI, dev containers, user sessions).
findings.counterexample: User runs 'flatpak remote-disable flathub' → next shell accessor call still returns cached 'enabled'

findings.description: False 'binary allowlist' claim in documentation. Claims 7 and 21 assert 'binary allowlist prevents PATH injection' but _flathub_validate_binary has NO allowlist — uses behavioral validation (--version regex + optional SHA-256). Misleads auditors.
findings.counterexample: Security audit checks for allowlist paths; finds only behavioral validation with optional SHA-256 pinning

findings.description: TOCTOU 'elimination' overclaim. realpath is GNU coreutils (absent on macOS <10.12, *BSD, busybox, distroless containers); mitigation only narrows window, doesn't eliminate. Fallback chain (realpath → readlink -f → original path) adds complexity.
findings.counterexample: macOS 10.11 / Alpine / distroless container → realpath missing, TOCTOU mitigation degrades silently

findings.description: Custom installations probe runs out of documented ladder order. _flathub_probe_installations executes unconditionally when binary exists, regardless of whether command path already found flathub. Violates 'first step that yields answer wins' architecture.
findings.counterexample: Command path finds flathub enabled in 'system' → custom installations probe still runs and may modify FLATHUB_SCOPE

findings.description: type -P usage for binary lookup is correct defensive practice — avoids aliases/functions, searches PATH only.
Debug redaction is exceptionally thorough — covers home dirs, runtime dirs, flatpak paths, NixOS, Homebrew (macOS/Linuxbrew), env vars, custom installations.
Double-source guard and direct-execution rejection are solid.
Source guard subshell pattern (return 0 2>/dev/null) || exit 0 handles bash -c/eval contexts correctly.

steelman: TOCTOU mitigation via dual validation (original path + canonical realpath) with fd-based atomic read is reference-grade for shell libraries
type -P for flatpak binary lookup is correct defensive practice, avoids alias/function resolution
Cache integrity verification with SHA-256 content hashes detects external state drift on binary and configs
Debug redaction is exceptionally thorough across platforms (home, nix store, homebrew, custom installations)
Double-source guard and direct-execution rejection are solid
Source guard subshell pattern handles bash -c/eval contexts correctly
Config parser correctly handles case-insensitive enabled=false values and fails safe to disabled
All globals always written, safe for set -u callers
counterArgument: Critical: Scope normalization silently drops custom installations — FLATHUB_SCOPE='empty' when Flathub ONLY in custom install (Steam Deck, Silverblue)
Critical: State machine treats query failure as 'no flathub' — returns 'not-configured' instead of 'unknown' on partial scope failure
Critical: Positive-only cache has no TTL/invalidation — stale ENABLED in long-lived shells after flatpak remote-disable
Critical: False 'binary allowlist' claim — no allowlist exists, only behavioral validation; misleads auditors
Critical: TOCTOU 'eliminated portably' but realpath missing on macOS <10.12, *BSD, busybox; narrows window only
Custom installations probe runs unconditionally, violating documented ladder order
Detection ladder conflates orthogonal strategies (binary presence, CLI output, config parsing, custom paths)

rationale.A: Critical functional defects in scope normalization (discards custom installations) and state machine (treats failures as 'not-configured') produce false negatives that undermine security posture. Positive-only caching without TTL creates stale-state risk in long-lived environments. Security claims around allowlist and TOCTOU elimination are overstated.
rationale.B: The library has strong defensive practices (type -P, SHA-256 cache integrity, debug redaction) but six convergent critical weaknesses undermine correctness: custom installations silently dropped in scope normalization, state machine treating partial failure as 'not-configured', detection ladder order violation, false allowlist claims misleading auditors, TOCTOU portability overclaim, and positive-only caching without invalidation. These are architectural flaws requiring fixes, not cosmetic issues.
rationale.C: The critical issues around silent custom installation drops (claim 3/17/20), false 'not-configured' on partial query failure (claim 15), and unbounded positive caching without invalidation create silent data corruption in production. These are not theoretical — they will cause flathub detection to return wrong answers in multi-installation environments (Steam Deck, Fedora Silverblue, custom Flatpak setups) and long-running CI/devcontainer sessions.
rationale.D: Six convergent critical weaknesses violate core specification claims: custom installations are silently discarded (Claim 3/17/20), state machine misclassifies query failures as 'not-configured' (Claim 15), ladder order is violated by unconditional custom probe (Claim 7/21), binary allowlist claim is false (Claim 7/21), TOCTOU elimination overclaims portability (Claim 8), and positive-only caching lacks invalidation (Claim 11). These are not implementation bugs but specification contract violations.
rationale.E: Six convergent critical findings violate core security claims and functional correctness. Scope normalization silently dropping custom installations (finding 1) and false 'not-configured' on partial failure (finding 2) produce false negatives that defeat the library's purpose. False allowlist claims (finding 4) and TOCTOU overstatement (finding 5) are material misrepresentations for audit trails. Positive-only caching without TTL (finding 6) causes compliance drift in long-lived environments.

recommendations: Fix _flathub_normalize_scope to preserve custom installation names in FLATHUB_SCOPE output
Fix state machine: query failure on one scope → 'unknown', not 'not-configured'
Add cache invalidation: TTL, signal handler, or explicit flathub_clear_cache() function
Correct documentation: replace 'binary allowlist' claims with 'behavioral validation + optional SHA-256 pinning'
Add realpath availability check; degrade TOCTOU claim to 'narrows window portably'
Make custom installations probe respect ladder order: only run if no earlier step found flathub
Consider adding flathub_clear_cache() for explicit invalidation by callers
